CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
MOLECULAR GENETICS REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Placental tissue (uncultured)
Specimen Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Referral Location: [redacted location]

CLINICAL INDICATION
DNA analysis requested on placental material from miscarriage. Fetal tissue submitted for chromosomal analysis.

TEST PERFORMED
1. Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
   - Platform: GeneScan G2000
   - Oligonucleotide array with approximately 60,000 genome-wide probes
   - Reference genome: GRCh37/hg19
   - Resolution: >1Mb for copy number changes

2. Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
   - Chromosomes analyzed: 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X, Y
   - Purpose: Rapid aneuploidy detection and triploidy exclusion

RESULTS

ARRAY CGH FINDINGS:
arr[GRCh37] Xp22.31(6,457,402-8,032,120)x0

A 1.575 Mb deletion was detected at Xp22.31 (genomic coordinates: 6,457,402-8,032,120)
Male chromosome complement (XY) with nullisomy for the deleted region
No other copy number imbalances >1Mb detected
No other regions of known pathogenicity identified

QF-PCR RESULTS:
Normal male pattern confirmed
No evidence of triploidy
No aneuploidy detected for chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22

GENES WITHIN DELETED REGION:
The deletion encompasses multiple genes including:
- STS (Steroid Sulfatase; OMIM 300747) - Complete deletion
- VCX3A, VCX2, VCX, PNPLA4, and additional genes

INTERPRETATION
The 1.575 Mb deletion at Xp22.31 results in complete loss of the STS gene. Hemizygous deletion of STS in males is associated with X-linked ichthyosis (OMIM 308100), a skin disorder characterized by dark, scaly skin. This condition typically presents in infancy or early childhood with generalized scaling, particularly prominent on the extensor surfaces.

While STS deletions can be associated with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorders in some cases, this deletion is unlikely to be the primary cause of the miscarriage. The majority of males with STS deletions have normal prenatal development and are born at term.

The deletion may be inherited from a carrier mother or may have arisen de novo. Carrier females are typically asymptomatic or may have mild manifestations.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Maternal blood sample is recommended for array CGH analysis to determine if the deletion was inherited
2. If maternal, the recurrence risk for future pregnancies would be 50% for male fetuses
3. Genetic counseling is strongly advised to discuss:
   - Inheritance pattern and recurrence risks
   - Clinical implications of X-linked ichthyosis
   - Prenatal testing options for future pregnancies
4. Consider additional investigations for other potential causes of miscarriage

This analysis was performed in accordance with laboratory standards and has been reviewed by qualified personnel.

Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name], Clinical Cytogeneticist
Laboratory Director: Dr. [redacted name]
